mechanism.name: static capacity allocation from the TRAIN graph's AF3 sign mix
mechanism.question: Can the sign distribution of the TRAIN graph's AF3 edge values decide, before training, how the 32 coordinates of each RQ-VAE level split into hyperbolic, Euclidean and spherical components, so the hard SID preserves behaviour-graph structure better?
mechanism.one_sentence: Level 1 stays E32; levels 2 and 3 split 32 coordinates into H x E x S by largest remainder of the AF3 sign proportions, then train the frozen RQ-VAE recipe once with no behaviour signal in the training path.
mechanism.distinct_from: M1 learns one curvature per level and M2 carries a radial coordinate inside the code; here nothing about the geometry is learned or carried by the code: the graph's sign mix only decides a fixed dimension budget before training, and AF3 is read once, outside the model.

computations.statement: For every canonical TRAIN edge (i, j): F_ij = 4 - d_i - d_j + 3 T_ij; count minus = #{F_ij < 0}, zero = #{F_ij = 0}, plus = #{F_ij > 0}. Frozen counts: 315391 edges, 315390 minus, 1 zero, 0 plus; proportions (0.9999968293324794, 3.170667520633119e-06, 0.0).

Largest remainder on 32 with order (H, E, S) and ties to the lower index. Level 1 is fixed at (0, 32, 0) by the issue. The frozen proportions give level 2 = level 3 = (32, 0, 0): H32, E0, S0. The sphere component is zero, so no sphere code path exists in this candidate; the rule is still exercised by tests on synthetic counts.
Per level, in its own space: Euclidean level cost = ||r - c||^2; hyperbolic level cost = d_c(r, exp_0(c))^2 / 4, with the repository convention d_0(x, y) = 2||x - y||. Curvature c = 1 is frozen.

Euclidean level: r' = r - c. Hyperbolic level: r' = project((-exp_0(c)) (+) r). Space transition E -> H uses exp_0(r); H -> H is the identity. A sphere transition would use the same exp/log pair but is unreachable because every d_S is zero.

phi(q) = q_E(L1) + log_0(exp_0(c_2) (+) exp_0(c_3)): the Euclidean level contributes its tangent code, the hyperbolic levels contribute the log of their nested ball sum. The result is 32-dimensional, the decoder input.

Nearest code on levels 1 and 2, the baseline's balanced Sinkhorn on level 3 during training, deterministic nearest code at export. The rule is the frozen baseline's; the cost matrix is the allocated one.
Rank-zero KMeans of the residual in the level's native tangent (Euclidean coordinates for E, log_0 coordinates for H), broadcast to every rank before the first step.

inputs.graph: the canonical TRAIN behaviour graph with F_ij = 4 - d_i - d_j + 3 T_ij (read once for the sign counts, never inside the model)

outputs.sid: three tokens per item plus the disambiguation token
outputs.geometry: the per-level (H, E, S) layout, frozen and recorded

learned: three codebooks of 256 x 32 (level 1 Euclidean, levels 2 and 3 hyperbolic)

gradient_rules.encoder: through the straight-through readout: the decoder sees phi(q), the encoder receives its gradient
gradient_rules.codebooks: each level's commitment (code detached) and codebook (residual detached) terms in its own cost
gradient_rules.residual: the chosen code is detached; the residual recursion carries no codebook gradient

training_integration.records: logs/training_metrics.jsonl carries one train event per epoch; the geometry is a frozen constant, so there is no per-epoch mechanism event

conventions.distance: d_0(x, y) = 2||x - y||; d_c(x, y) = 2 atanh(sqrt(c)||(-x) (+) y||)/sqrt(c)
conventions.curvature: kappa = -c, c = 1; the ball is {x : c|x|^2 < 1}
conventions.readout: phi is the 32-d tangent vector the decoder reconstructs from

switches.GEOMETRY_OFF: all levels E32, the frozen baseline's geometry; only a cheap wiring check, never trained
switches.BEHAVIOUR_ON: not applicable: AF3 never enters forward, loss, sampling or gradients in this issue
switches.policy: no arm with a switch off is trained

excluded.surface: the sign counting and the largest-remainder allocation
the assignment and the Sinkhorn balancing
excluded.reason: discrete; the rule is the baseline's
the frozen baseline's own surface, verified by its tree

excluded.surface: the 32-dimensional norm inside the hyperbolic cost
excluded.reason: the symbolic contract states the width-1 surface; the callable applies the same formula to the norm, exercised numerically
the frozen allocation gives every d_S = 0; no sphere code path exists in this candidate

continuous_surface.note: The width-1 form of d_c(r, exp_0(q))^2/4 at c = 1: Möbius subtraction in one dimension. The trained implementation applies the same expression to the norm of the 32-d residual and code; that norm form is excluded from the symbolic comparison and covered by tests/test_math.py.
